entries: Materials and handling | Moving, transferring and stacking | Move raw materials, finished products and packed items manually or with hoists, and transfer finished goods, raw materials, tools and equipment between storage and work areas.

Feeding and unloading | Loading, removing and preparing materials | Load and unload items from machines, conveyors and vehicles, remove products, attachments or waste from machines, and prepare raw materials and feed them into machine hoppers according to procedures.

Production assistance | Assisting operation and positioning products | Operate production machinery or assist machine operators, start machines or equipment, and position products for further processing, inspection or packaging.

Inspection and identification | Marking, counting and inspection | Mark or tag parts, count finished products to determine whether orders are complete, examine products for conformity to quality standards, and sort by weight, grade and size.

Cleaning and records | Cleaning, packing and readings | Clean work areas, machines, equipment and products, pack and store materials and products, and take readings and record data, quantities and time.

Safety and collaboration | Equipment and lifting safeguards | If safeguards fail, equipment or lifting conditions are abnormal, or the assignment is unclear, helpers stop, step clear and tell the site lead. Keep original records within the assigned role. Where hazardous-energy control applies to servicing or maintenance, trained, authorized personnel isolate and verify the equipment and determine when it can return to service.

paragraphs:
Workplace and environment | Mainly factories, production lines and storage areas; commonly work around production lines, equipment and storage areas (O*NET work context and tasks; same coverage below).
Protection and exposure | Common hazardous equipment exposure (56% daily), common contaminant exposure (74% daily), common machinery and production noise, and vibration from machines and handheld tools.
Physical demands and posture | Prolonged standing (51% continually or almost continually, 13% more than half the time); commonly work around production lines, equipment and storage areas; moderate physical proximity (47% at arm's length, 15% slightly close).
Communication and collaboration | Close collaboration with operators and production-line coworkers (47% in constant contact with others); frequent face-to-face discussions (83% daily).
Accuracy and responsibility | High accuracy requirements (66% extremely important); serious consequences of error (21% extremely serious, 28% very serious); substantial responsibility for others' health and safety (39% very high responsibility, 31% high responsibility).
Progress and pace | Constrained by production plans, pace and orders; 80% of O*NET respondents report needing to meet strict deadlines daily. Ask the employer about line speed and rotation.
Equipment and materials | Machines, conveyors, hoisting and handling equipment, materials and finished products.
Scheduling and site | Mostly regular schedules (67% regular, 33% irregular); mainly teamwork; schedules are mostly regular and vary with production and contract periods (67% regular, 33% irregular).
Automation | Moderately low automation (38% moderately automated, 35% not at all automated).

Records and collaboration | Starting with production work orders, drawings or process cards and materials lists, first check product and work order identifiers; materials, parts and specifications; feeding, unloading and handling; machine operation observation; marking and counting; inspection and sorting; energy isolation and protection; and post-work cleaning, organization and records. Then assist according to operators' instructions and production pace and hand over by shift. Energy isolation, lockout/tagout, hoisting, machinery, chemicals and confined spaces must follow qualification requirements and procedures, with traceable production and inspection records retained.

BLS wage coverage presented by O*NET | This page covers O*NET/SOC 51-9198.00, Helpers--Production Workers. O*NET's 51-9198.00 page presents 2025 U.S. median wages of USD 18.78 per hour / USD 39,070 per year (2025, BLS OEWS, data for this occupation itself, 51-9198.00). The 10th percentile is USD 14.97 per hour and USD 31,140 per year; the 25th is USD 16.93 per hour and USD 35,220 per year; the 75th is USD 22.11 per hour and USD 45,990 per year; and the 90th is USD 25.68 per hour and USD 53,410 per year. All come from BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS 2025, as presented by O*NET). The page does not mark them as coming from a broader or neighboring occupation, so they are presented as data for this occupation itself (51-9198.00). They include production bonuses and other specified wage components and exclude overtime pay, shift differentials, nonproduction bonuses and employer benefit costs; the median is not an entry-level starting wage. Boundary conclusion | This page covers O*NET 51-9198.00, Helpers--Production Workers. Its central distinction from neighboring roles is work objects, outputs and authorization levels. It deals with equipment, production lines, materials, finished goods and on-site assistance, producing assistance completed according to work orders and procedures—materials, feeding, handling, inspection, counting and cleaning—and traceable production and inspection records. Workers use materials, equipment and site coordination skills within operators' instructions and job authorization, taking responsibility for work safety, production quality and site order. Team Assemblers, machine feeders, packaging machine operators, inspectors and hand material movers produce work in their own specialties, with different responsibility and authorization levels.

Core principle of neighboring roles | Most related and neighboring roles aim to complete production, assembly, packaging or inspection to specified quality within procedural and safety requirements, with records retained. Differences concern work objects, outputs and authorization levels: some focus on independent operation, assembly and inspection, while others focus on on-site assistance, materials and cleaning.

Core purpose of this occupation | Work with equipment, production lines, materials, finished goods, work orders and procedures within operators' instructions, safety requirements and authorization: materials and handling, feeding and unloading, production assistance, inspection, identification and counting, and cleaning, packing and records. Outputs are assistance meeting procedures and traceable records.

Main work objects and bases of neighboring roles | Team Assemblers follow assembly and manufacturing procedures; machine feeders and offbearers follow feeding and unloading procedures; packaging machine operators follow packaging and filling procedures; inspectors and sorters follow inspection and sampling standards; hand material movers follow handling and storage procedures. Most focus on independent operation, assembly, inspection or handling, unlike this occupation's on-site production assistance.

Main work objects and bases of this occupation | Work with product and work order identifiers, materials, parts and specifications, feeding, unloading and handling, machine operation observation, marking and counting, inspection and sorting, energy isolation and protection, and cleaning, organization and record requirements. Provide assistance and make judgments according to procedures, current acceptance standards, work safety and occupational health requirements.

Occupational profile | Helpers--Production Workers corresponds to O*NET51-9198.00, supplying or holding materials and tools, cleaning work areas and equipment, and providing production assistance through handling, identification, counting, initial inspection, observing equipment and reporting malfunctions. Site operation scope is determined by job training and authorization. Work may involve machine operation, rather than only handling and cleaning, but does not automatically confer equipment or quality release authority.

Core processes of neighboring roles | Team Assemblers focus on assembly and fabrication; machine feeders and offbearers on feeding and unloading; packaging machine operators on packaging and filling; inspectors and sorters on inspection, sampling and sorting; this occupation on assistance with materials, feeding, handling, inspection and cleaning.

Core process of this occupation | Receive work orders and check materials; check task assignments and safeguards; feed, unload and handle materials; observe machine operation and assist operation; inspect, count and identify; and clean, pack, record and hand over. Every step must follow work orders, procedures and operators' instructions and be open to review by operators, quality inspectors and safety personnel.

Main outputs of neighboring roles | Team Assemblers produce assemblies and fabrication records; machine feeders and offbearers produce feeding, unloading and output records; packaging machine operators produce packaged goods and packaging records; inspectors and sorters produce inspection, sorting and conformity determination records. These differ from this occupation's assistance and production and inspection records.

Main outputs of this occupation | Assistance completed according to work orders and procedures: handled and fed materials and finished goods, identified and counted products, inspected and sorted batches, and cleaned and organized sites. Outputs also include production, inspection and counting records; consumption and rework records; abnormalities and outstanding items; and traceable shift and handover records.

Responsibility in neighboring roles | Responsibility in related and neighboring roles is usually defined by the employer and production, safety and quality systems, primarily concerning product quality, personal safety, production continuity and the site environment.

Workers in this occupation are responsible for their own feeding, handling, inspection, counting, identification, cleaning and records, and assistance completed according to work orders, procedures and safety requirements. Energy isolation, critical equipment operation, special equipment, hoisting and handling, and major quality and safety matters must be referred to appropriate roles or organizations according to qualifications, job authorization and procedures.

Authority and approvals in neighboring roles | Authority in related and neighboring roles comes from enterprise authorization and production, safety and professional standards. It usually excludes independent decisions on process or formulation changes, critical equipment parameters and major responses. Process changes, equipment modifications, special equipment and major rework should be referred to appropriate roles or organizations.

Authority and approvals in this occupation | Routine feeding, handling, inspection, counting and cleaning must remain within operators' instructions, job authorization and work order procedures. Energy isolation, lockout/tagout, hoisting, handling, critical equipment operation, process changes and major rework must follow procedures and qualification requirements. Qualifications and work permits for hoisting, special equipment and hazardous work are subject to competent authority and enterprise requirements.

Limits on conclusions in neighboring roles | Conclusions in related and neighboring roles are mostly limited to the relevant process or batch and generally do not determine product quality, equipment safety or legal liability. Conclusions spanning specialties or involving special equipment and major safety issues have limits on their applicability.

Limits on conclusions in this occupation | Feeding, handling, inspection, counting and identification conclusions should state only verifiable records, work performed and results, distinguishing measured facts, judgments and inferences, and matters awaiting verification. Workers must not issue conclusions in their own name on matters beyond their qualifications, such as special equipment inspections, quality conformity determinations or accident determinations.

Checks before joining | Use the following six items when applying and before starting work, to avoid inferring actual duties and authority from job titles or promotional wording. Base findings on written recruitment information, employment contracts, job descriptions, and production and safety procedures, and keep confirming them after joining. This page lists checks only and does not constitute a hiring or safety determination.

Check guidance | Similar job titles may have very different duties and authority. Some focus on handling, feeding and cleaning; others on inspection, counting and sorting; others on specific lines such as assembly, processing, packaging or storage; and some also involve machine operation and hoisting assistance. Specialized work, qualification and safety requirements vary by enterprise and jurisdiction. Check them before assessing fit.

01 Actual duties, work and site authority | Check whether the role actually provides feeding, unloading, handling, inspection and counting assistance, or mainly cleaning and support. Confirm permitted lines and processes, such as assembly, processing, packaging or storage; authority to use tools, equipment and hoisting and handling equipment; authorization for energy isolation and critical equipment operation; and interfaces with operators, crews, quality inspectors and safety personnel.

Check guidance | This occupation commonly works around dust, contaminants, noise, production pace and heat or cold and involves machinery and hoisting risks. It generally requires training in safety, energy isolation, lockout/tagout, hoisting, handling, machinery, dust, chemicals and occupational health, with compliance with personal protection and emergency response requirements.

02 Safety, occupational health, machinery and energy isolation requirements | Check whether the employer requires and provides safe operating procedures and energy isolation, lockout/tagout, machinery and hoisting training; hoisting, special equipment and hazardous work permit requirements; personal protection, emergency response and drills; handling and reporting requirements for waste, wastewater, dust and noise; and requirements to identify and report equipment and site hazards.

For mainland China material staging and line-side delivery roles, look for production material clerk postings. Check whether the job also involves equipment, counting or inspection, and who authorizes those duties.

03 Education, training, on-the-job training and qualification requirements | Check whether vocational school training or on-the-job experience is required (the page lists Job Zone 1-2, little or no preparation to some preparation needed, and SVP below 6.0, SVP Below 6.0); whether on-the-job training or skilled-worker mentoring is offered; whether hoisting, special equipment, machine operation or hazardous work requires qualifications, internal training or assessment; and whether training and assessment cover feeding, handling, inspection, counting, cleaning, safety and emergency response.

Check guidance | This occupation focuses on handling, physical activity, identification and evaluation. Its highest-rated activities are handling and moving objects 87, performing general physical activities 84, identifying objects, actions, and events 72, and evaluating information to determine compliance with standards 71. Hazardous equipment, contaminants and noise are common, time pressure is high (80% daily), accuracy requirements are high, consequences of error are serious, and responsibility for others' health and safety is substantial. Include site conditions, physical demands and tolerance for safety-related demands in your checks.

04 Pay, working hours and employment contract definitions | Check compensation components: base pay; overtime, shift, night-shift and heat allowances; piece rates and crew performance pay; regional, enterprise and production-line differences; the five social insurance schemes and housing provident fund; labor protection, protective supplies, meals and accommodation. Confirm hours, schedules, rotating shifts and peak-season overtime, contract duration, probation and termination terms, and training, qualification and advancement arrangements. U.S. medians and percentiles are market references only, not any enterprise's or region's offer.

Check guidance | Interfaces with operators, crews, production lines, quality inspectors, equipment personnel and safety personnel determine feeding, inspection, acceptance, authority, responsibility and disclosure boundaries and must be clarified beforehand.

05 Interfaces with operators, crews and production lines | Confirm authority to approve and adjust materials, feeding and counts; arrangements for requesting, using and reviewing tools, equipment and hoisting and handling equipment; processes for feeding, inspection, counting, nonconformities and rework; and requirements for handling and externally providing enterprise, customer and equipment manufacturer technical information.

Check guidance | Traceability and recordkeeping requirements for work orders, materials, feeding, handling, inspection, counting, cleaning and abnormalities determine quality and responsibility boundaries. Clarify templates, deadlines, amendment, archiving, access and retention rules beforehand. Enterprise, customer and equipment manufacturer technical information must also follow confidentiality and minimum-necessary requirements.

06 Materials, production, quality and record requirements | Check requirements for work order records; materials, specifications and quantities used; feeding, unloading and handling; machine operation observation; marking and counting; inspection and sorting; cleaning, organization, abnormalities, rework and outstanding items; and work permits, shift handovers, original records and revision trails.

paragraphs: Conclusion | The central distinction between this page's O*NET 51-9198.00 Helpers--Production Workers and neighboring roles concerns work objects, outputs and authorization levels. This occupation works with equipment, production lines, materials, finished goods and on-site assistance, producing assistance completed according to work orders and procedures and traceable production and inspection records. Team Assemblers, machine feeders, packaging machine operators, inspectors and hand material movers focus on their own work objects, with different outputs and authorization levels.

Evidence note | The occupations compared below come from O*NET classifications and public sources. The comparison helps distinguish neighboring occupations' work and assess fit. It does not constitute qualification, hiring or pay conclusions, or safety, special equipment or legal advice. Check wages and employment using each occupation's own code and statistical coverage; figures cannot be transferred between occupations.

Introduction | The comparison below uses four columns: occupational direction—core work and outputs—key distinction—who may prefer it. Assembly, feeding, packaging, inspection and handling roles often connect within the same production line and process, but coordination does not make them interchangeable. Their work objects, equipment, qualifications and responsibility boundaries differ and must be checked separately.

Key distinction: this occupation works with equipment, production lines, materials, finished goods and on-site assistance. Using materials, equipment and site coordination skills, workers complete feeding, handling, inspection, counting and cleaning within operators' instructions and job authorization, taking responsibility for work safety, production quality and site order. Neighboring roles focus on independent assembly, feeding, packaging, inspection or handling, with different specialties and authority.

May better suit people willing to provide hands-on assistance with materials, equipment and production lines, perform feeding, handling, inspection, counting and cleaning thoroughly according to operators' instructions and work orders, and accept responsibility for work safety and production quality.

Core work and outputs: move raw materials, finished products and packed items manually or with hoists; load and unload machines and conveyors; observe equipment and promptly report malfunctions; mark parts; count finished products and check conformity to quality standards; sort by weight, grade and size; and clean work areas and equipment and record data. Outputs are assistance completed according to work orders and procedures and production and inspection records.
This occupation: Helpers--Production Workers (O*NET/SOC 51-9198.00, Helpers--Production Workers)
Key distinction: focuses on independent assembly and fabrication, producing assemblies and fabrication records. This occupation focuses on on-site assistance, with a different authorization level.
May better suit people willing to take independent responsibility for assembly and fabrication; this occupation emphasizes on-site assistance with materials, feeding, handling and inspection.
Core work and outputs: assembling, fabricating and inspecting parts and semi-finished products, producing assemblies and fabrication and inspection records.
Team Assemblers (Team Assemblers, 51-2092.00)
Key distinction: focuses on feeding and unloading, producing feeding and unloading records. This occupation focuses on broader production-line assistance, with a different responsibility scope.
May better suit people willing to specialize in feeding and unloading; this occupation emphasizes combined materials, inspection and cleaning assistance on production lines.
Core work and outputs: feeding machines and removing finished products and waste, producing feeding, unloading and output records.
Machine Feeders and Offbearers (Machine Feeders and Offbearers, 53-7063.00)
Key distinction: focuses on packaging and filling equipment operation, producing packaged goods and records. This occupation focuses on on-site assistance, with a different authorization level.
May better suit people willing to operate and tend packaging and filling equipment; this occupation emphasizes materials, handling and inspection assistance in packaging.
Core work and outputs: operating, tending, adjusting and inspecting packaging and filling equipment, producing packaged goods and packaging records.
Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders (Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders, 51-9111.00)

Key distinction: focuses on independent inspection, sorting and conformity determinations, producing inspection determination records. This occupation focuses on on-site assistance and initial inspection, with a different authorization level.
May better suit people willing to specialize in inspection and sorting; this occupation emphasizes counting, initial inspection and identification within production assistance.
Core work and outputs: inspecting, testing, sorting, sampling and weighing products and materials, producing inspection, sorting and conformity determination records.
Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers (Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers, 51-9061.00)
Key distinction: focuses on manual handling and storage, producing handling and storage records. This occupation focuses on production-line assistance, with different settings and duties.
May better suit people willing to perform manual handling and storage; this occupation emphasizes combined feeding, inspection and cleaning assistance on production lines.
Core work and outputs: manual handling, storage, loading, unloading and stacking, producing handling, storage, loading and unloading records.
Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand (Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand, 53-7062.00)

Transition | This page places neighboring roles side by side by work objects, outputs and authorization levels to help you decide which assembly, feeding, packaging, inspection or handling work you want to pursue over time. In every direction, actual readiness depends on the relevant equipment, procedures, safety and qualification capabilities, together with the target enterprise's and jurisdiction's training, specialized work and qualification requirements.
